reviews.author: David Hildenbrand (Arm)
reviews.summary: Identified pte_none_or_zero() as a poorly designed function, suggesting it be replaced with more specific helpers like pte_is_zero_page(). The author agreed to drop the original function and add a new one that aligns with existing naming conventions.

2026-08-16.patch_summary: This RFC patch proposes adding a new function, pte_none_or_zero(), to the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) subsystem. The function is intended to simplify code that needs to handle page table entries (PTEs) that either map nothing or the shared zeropage. The patch also includes minor changes to existing code in khugepaged.c and migrate_device.c to use this new function.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: Agreed to David's suggestion, dropping the original function and adding a new one that follows existing naming conventions.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Aug 17, 2026 at 07:57:29PM +0200, David Hildenbrand (Arm) wrote:
> And let the callers still spell both cases out.
> 
> if (pte_none(pte) || pte_is_zero_page(pte))
> 	/* Do something amazing */

Works for me.  I will drop pte_none_or_zero() and add pte_is_zero_page(),
which lines up with is_zero_page() in mm.h.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
